findings.title: Dependency contract in §2/§2.1 is partly wrong and not reproducible from the repo
findings.problem: §2 claims typer 0.25.x is pinned by yolov5 -> roboflow -> typer<0.26 and that uv lock verified 131 packages with opencv-python-headless 5.0.0.93 and typer 0.25.1. Repo pyproject.toml declares only typer>=0.12 and uv.lock has 9 packages pinning typer 0.27.2. A real py3.12 resolution of the intended set yields 115 packages, roboflow 1.3.8 (no typer cap) -> typer 0.27.2, and opencv-python-headless 4.10.0.84. Since §2.1 states uv run syncs the venv to pyproject+lock, the first uv sync will replace the exact environment (torch 2.14.0 / torchvision 0.29.0 / timm 1.0.29) in which RECON verified MegaDetector loading, MegaDetector inference and both backbone loads.
findings.fix: Pin the verified environment explicitly in [project.dependencies] (typer==0.27.2, torch==2.14.0, torchvision==0.29.0, timm==1.0.29, yolov5==7.0.14, opencv-python-headless==5.0.0.93, pillow==12.3.0, pillow-heif>=1.1.1, fastapi==0.141.1, uvicorn[standard]==0.39.0, httpx==0.28.1, setuptools<81), keep the [tool.uv] override-dependencies opencv-python removal, commit uv.lock, require uv sync --frozen, and delete the typer<0.26 claim (or additionally pin roboflow==1.3.8 to make it deterministic). Add a rule: if a resolution moves torch/torchvision/timm, re-run the three probe scripts and update RECON before proceeding.

findings.title: Label for a degenerate dominant box is undefined; species_or_unknown() is never defined
findings.problem: §5.3 keeps sub-2px boxes out of classification (species=NULL, species_status='degenerate') but counts them for dominance; §5.7 then calls species_or_unknown(animals[0]) on such a box. That function is never defined, so both 'unknown' and a crash on None < 0.45 are reachable. Real data hits this: instances_val2017.json has 7 non-crowd animal boxes under 2px in one dimension, min area_frac 0.000012.
findings.fix: Define species_or_unknown in §5.7: degenerate or species_conf is None -> 'unknown'; species_conf < min_species_confidence -> 'unknown'; else slug(species_common). Add E26: classify --detector scripted with a 1px animal box as the only detection asserts label 'unknown', boxes.species_status='degenerate', file materialized under unknown/, exit 0.

findings.title: BirdResult, GpsPoint and Prediction.top5 referenced but never defined
findings.problem: The BirdProvider protocol returns BirdResult with no field list and no rule for merging it into boxes/candidates/model_id; Prediction.top5 element shape is never stated although the candidates table needs rank/common/scientific/score.
findings.fix: Add dataclasses for GpsPoint, Candidate(rank, common, scientific, score) and BirdResult(provider, status in {refined,kept_coarse,unreachable,no_gps}, prediction | None), plus the merge rule: on 'refined' replace boxes.species_* and candidates with the bird head's top-5 and set images.model_id='<species_id>+<bird_id>'; otherwise keep the coarse row and write only provider_status.

findings.title: Bird refinement is unreachable as E8 specifies it, because the trigger is the coarse head's top-1
findings.problem: Refinement fires only when a box's coarse top-1 rolls up to Aves. E8 trains a 5-species CUB head and classifies a CUB image without saying which species artifact is loaded; the only artifact the suite builds is E7's 6-class COCO subset, which need not contain 'bird'. If the coarse head lacks bird or misranks a warbler, own_bird_head is never invoked and E8 fails for an unrelated reason.
findings.fix: Require the 10-class COCO head for E8 (or mandate 'bird' in the E7 subset when reused); widen the trigger to 'any of the coarse top-3 rolls up to Aves, or coarse top-1 below min_species_confidence with any Aves entry in top-3'; add a documented --force-bird-head diagnostic flag so E8 can exercise the bird head independently.

findings.title: E4 has no pass criterion and compares MegaDetector boxes to COCO ground-truth expectations
findings.problem: 'Images COCO says have a clear area winner get that species; images with ratio < 1.5 get multiple' is not decidable: MegaDetector's box set differs from the annotator's (missed small animals, merged herds, unannotated animals, excluded person/vehicle boxes), so per-image equality will be flaky. Recomputed at the design's own 1.6 gate, the 471 multi-animal images split 235 dominant / 236 multiple, so 'clear winner' is not a small safe subset either.
findings.fix: Freeze a list (tests/e2e/data/coco_dominance.json: first 40 ids with GT ratio > 3.0 and first 40 with ratio < 1.3, sorted) and assert aggregates: every label in the closed set; >= 32/40 of the high-ratio set not 'multiple'; >= 32/40 of the low-ratio set 'multiple'; print the counts. Assert species identity in E7, not E4.

findings.title: No guarantee against train/test leakage between the COCO-trained species model and E4/E7
findings.problem: The species model trains on COCO val2017 and E4/E7 evaluate on COCO val2017. The sha1(path) split is deterministic, but no section requires the e2e assertion images to come from the val bucket, so the natural implementation reports accuracy on trained-on images and E7's 'beats chance' assertion becomes meaningless.
findings.fix: Publish split_for(path) = 'val' if int(sha1(path),16) % 5 == 0 else 'train' as the single source of truth in §7.2; require E4 and E7 to assert split_for(path) == 'val' for every asserted image and to filter the training manifest to split == 'train'.

findings.title: E7 and E10 accuracy thresholds are unspecified
findings.problem: 'val top-1 beats the 1/6 chance floor by a margin asserted numerically' never states the margin, and E10 says only 'accuracy above chance'. The implementer must invent both numbers and neither is reviewable.
findings.fix: E7: 6 classes (zebra, elephant, giraffe, bear, cow, sheep), train-split crops only, --input-size 128 --epochs-head 2 --epochs-finetune 2 --batch-size 32; assert val_top1 >= 0.55, artifact train.val_top1 == metrics.json top-1 within 1e-6, runtime < 20 min on 8 CPU cores. E10: 4 synthetic classes, 500 train / 100 val, assert val_top1 >= 0.90 and runtime < 90 s.

findings.title: E16's HEIC fixture cannot be produced: pi-heif cannot encode HEIF
findings.problem: data/raw contains only JPEG corpora, so the fixture builder must encode a HEIC file. Verified in-sandbox: pi_heif 1.4.0 im.save(format='HEIF') raises KeyError: 'HEIF' (decode works). The design never states how the HEIC fixture is created, so the format-policy test is unbuildable.
findings.fix: Use pillow-heif (decode superset of pi-heif plus the x265 encoder; verified pillow_heif 1.1.1 / libheif 1.20.2 encodes and re-reads a HEIF file) as the runtime dependency, as PLAN.md originally specified, and state that make_e2e_fixtures.py writes the HEIC fixture by re-encoding a COCO JPEG and FAILS loudly if HEIF encoding is unavailable rather than skipping E16. Do not substitute AVIF.

findings.title: The formats config key has no defined semantics, no validation and no CLI flag
findings.problem: §3 ships formats = [jpeg, png, tiff, heic] but §5.1 states the extension policy as a hardcoded allowlist and §10.2 never validates the key. Whether removing 'heic' skips .heic files, and whether adding 'raw' substitutes for --raw, are both guessable and unstated.
findings.fix: Define formats as the eligible-family selector with entries constrained to jpeg|png|tiff|heic (unknown value -> fatal exit 3 listing the valid set); a file whose family is not listed is skipped with a new enumerated reason format_disabled; RAW remains governed solely by --raw; expose --formats as a repeatable classify flag; add a --formats jpeg case to E16.

findings.title: source_root has no provenance for the gui and verify commands
findings.problem: §6 permits serving bytes from 'source_root ... for a --dry-run catalog' and §8's verify checks output_root is 'not nested with a source', but both commands take only -o/--output and no schema column holds a source root. Neither check is implementable as written.
findings.fix: Add runs.source_root TEXT NOT NULL written at run start; gui and verify read it from the latest runs row. With no runs row, verify reports the nesting check as skipped(no_runs) and the GUI serves /full only from output_root, returning 409 'image was planned by --dry-run and has no materialized file' for status='planned' rows (removing the read-only source-serving mode entirely).

findings.title: Catalog single-writer rule lets a GUI re-tag abort a running classify
findings.problem: §9 assumes a single writer while §6 exposes GET /api/run and POST .../label precisely so the GUI is usable during a run; §10.1 makes 'database is locked' fatal exit 1 after 3 retries, so re-tagging during a 2.8 h run can abort it, contradicting §10.1's own rule that a per-image failure never aborts the run.
findings.fix: GUI GET routes open the catalog with sqlite3.connect('file:...?mode=ro', uri=True); the re-tag POST uses a short write connection and returns 409 {'error': 'a classify run is writing the catalog; retry'} on contention, changing nothing on disk. In classify, lock contention retries with 0.5/1/2/4/8 s backoff and then records a per-image failed row (exit 4), never a fatal exit 1. Add the 409 path to E19.

findings.title: --device cuda with no CUDA device is unspecified, inviting a silent CPU substitution
findings.problem: --device [auto|cpu|cuda] is offered on classify and train, but no row in §10.1/§10.2 covers an explicit --device cuda on a machine where torch.cuda.is_available() is false. Falling back to CPU silently would violate invariant I7.
findings.fix: Add to §10.2: auto -> cuda if available else cpu, logged at INFO and stored in runs.config_json; cuda when unavailable -> fatal exit 3 with '--device cuda requested but torch reports no available CUDA device; omit the flag or pass --device cpu'; cpu always valid.

findings.title: ebird_enrich behaviour with no GPS is unspecified and 'down-rank' has no numeric definition
findings.problem: GPS is optional per §5.2, but §5.6 defines the provider in terms of the EXIF GPS point without saying what happens when it is absent, and 'down-ranks species that do not occur near the point' leaves the re-ranked top-1 (hence the filed label) implementation-defined.
findings.fix: Specify: no GPS -> canonicalize names only, provider_status='no_gps', ranking unchanged. With GPS -> one cached call to /v2/data/obs/geo/recent?lat&lng&dist=50&back=30; multiply the score of candidates absent from the response by 0.25, re-sort, then re-apply min_species_confidence (a demoted top-1 may become unknown). Add a no_gps assertion to E23.

findings.title: eval --calibrate mutates the artifact in place, breaking model_id traceability
findings.problem: §7.4 writes the fitted temperature into the artifact while §7.1 promises model_id lets any historical label be traced to the exact model that produced it. After calibration two behaviourally different models share one model_id and every pre-calibration images row points at a model that no longer exists.
findings.fix: eval --calibrate --out <new.acmodel> writes a copy with temperature set, model_id = f'{old}+cal{n}' and train.calibrated_from = old_model_id; writing calibration into an existing artifact path is refused (fatal exit 3). Artifacts are immutable once their model_id has been recorded.

findings.title: --ignore-overrides leaves ambiguous state that can flip labels and move files on a later run
findings.problem: It is not stated whether --ignore-overrides deletes overrides rows. If they survive, the next plain --reclassify re-applies the human label and moves the file back; if they are deleted, a flag named 'ignore' destroys the user's corrections.
findings.fix: State that --ignore-overrides never deletes overrides rows: it suppresses them for the current run and sets label_source='model'; a later run without the flag re-applies the newest override and moves the file back (intended and idempotent). Permanently discarding a correction requires a GUI re-tag. Extend E20 with a third run asserting the human label and destination return.

findings.title: Conflict: §5.8 says a crashed re-tag is reconciled, §8 gives verify no way to reconcile
findings.problem: §5.8 accepts an image present in two label dirs because 'the next classify or verify run reconciles' it, but §8's verify only checks and reports (no --fix) and classify skips status='done' hashes, so nothing ever reconciles and the duplicate is permanent.
findings.fix: Add verify --fix: where a row's label disagrees with a copy found under another label directory and an overrides row justifies the current label, delete the stale copy under the old label (never anything under source) and log it; without --fix, report only and exit non-zero. Extend E24 to simulate the interrupted re-tag and assert verify non-zero, verify --fix zero, one remaining copy, source tree untouched.

findings.title: --limit semantics against a resumed run are ambiguous
findings.problem: It is unstated whether --limit caps candidates scanned or images newly processed. Under the first reading a second classify --limit 100 processes zero new images (all already done), the opposite of §9's claim that --limit and resume make a 5,000-image card tolerable.
findings.fix: State that --limit N caps images newly submitted to inference; hashes already at status='done' are skipped without consuming budget, so repeated --limit runs advance through the card. Assert it in E13: two --limit 2 runs over a 5-image fixture produce 4 done rows.

findings.title: taxon_rank from PLAN's classifier contract was dropped
findings.problem: PLAN specifies {common_name, scientific_name, taxon_rank, confidence}; the .acmodel label entries carry class but no rank, so a coarse label (bird, cow) is indistinguishable in catalog and GUI from a species-level identification.
findings.fix: Add "rank": "species"|"class"|"order" to each artifact label entry plus a boxes.species_rank column, and show it in the GUI detail caption.

findings.title: Tool-internal dotfiles under output_root are not excluded from label enumeration
findings.problem: .catalog.db, .thumbs/, .ebird-cache.json and stale .ac-tmp-* all live under output_root, but nothing states that GET /api/labels and verify's orphan scan must ignore them.
findings.fix: State once in §5.8: label directories match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$; every other entry under output_root is tool-internal and ignored by the GUI and by verify.

findings.title: sources table needs an explicit upsert rule for a path whose content changed
findings.problem: sources(path PRIMARY KEY) with a sha256 FK: if a file is replaced in place, the same path arrives with a new hash and the insert conflicts.
findings.fix: Specify INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(path) DO UPDATE SET sha256=excluded.sha256, mtime_ns=excluded.mtime_ns, and note that the previous images row (and its destination file) is retained because content, not path, is the identity.

findings.title: Blur metric upscales images smaller than 512 px, biasing them toward junk
findings.problem: Resizing so the long edge is 'exactly 512 px' interpolates small images upward, depressing Laplacian variance and pushing small sharp animal-free photos toward junk.
findings.fix: Resize only when the long edge exceeds 512 px; measure smaller images as-is and store blur_ref_edge alongside blur_score.

findings.title: Collision check in link mode can hash through a dangling symlink
findings.problem: The already_present check hashes the existing destination's content; in link mode that dereferences a symlink whose target may be gone (card unplugged), which is unspecified.
findings.fix: In link mode compare os.readlink(dest) to the intended absolute source before hashing; replace a dangling destination symlink via the same atomic temp+os.replace path and count it as relinked.

findings.title: Unreachable error branch: pi_heif is a core dependency but §10.1 has a fatal 'pi_heif missing' row
findings.problem: With HEIC in the default format set and the HEIF library declared as a core dependency, the 'missing pi_heif' fatal branch can never execute.
findings.fix: Delete the row, keeping pillow-heif core (consistent with finding 8).

findings.title: '~2,700 instances' is 2,666 after the design's own iscrowd filter
findings.problem: Verified from instances_val2017.json: 2,700 animal annotations, 34 with iscrowd=1, 2,666 usable across 1,016 images (bird 427, sheep 354, cow 372, horse 272, zebra 266, elephant 252, giraffe 232, dog 218, cat 202, bear 71).
findings.fix: Quote 2,666 and note that bear (71 instances, ~14 in val) is the class that limits any per-class recall claim.

findings.title: Person-only photos filing as landscape needs user-facing documentation
findings.problem: The reasoning follows the closed taxonomy, but a card of family photos filed under landscape/ will surprise the user, and only the design explains why.
findings.fix: Add one line to the README and to classify's help text: images containing only people or vehicles are filed as landscape (or junk if blurry); their person/vehicle boxes are kept in the catalog and drawn in the GUI.
